DETERMINISTIC UNIT-CIRCLE VISUAL
The circle x²+y²=1 has cardinal points (1,0),(0,1),(−1,0),(0,−1) and the 120° point (−1/2,√3/2).
All plotted points satisfy x²+y²=1; cosine is the horizontal coordinate.
DESMOS STRATEGY
Enter x²+y²=1 and y=√3 x only for a verified reference line, or evaluate cos(120°) directly.
Look for the 120° terminal x-coordinate −0.5. For exact values, reference-angle reasoning is faster.
COMMON MISTAKES
Do not confuse cosine with y, mix radians and degrees, or lose the negative sign in Quadrants II and III.
The sign of cosine depends on x, not on whether the angle exceeds 90° alone.
EXAM STRATEGY
Reduce angles modulo 360°, identify the quadrant and reference angle, then select the x-coordinate sign.
For a known sine coordinate, use x²=1−y² and the quadrant to choose ±x.
QUICK CHECK
Find cos150° and cos300° without a calculator.
LESSON RECAP
Cosine is x on the unit circle. Quadrants I and IV have positive cosine; II and III have negative cosine.
x²+y²=1, cos²θ+sin²θ=1, and reference angles determine exact magnitudes.
